scenarios.name: Optimistic (best case, high team efficiency, low rework)

nonLabourLines.description: Stripe integration fees/sandbox testing & PCI review (one-off)
Legacy Oracle migration tooling / temporary read-replica infra
CI/CD and staging cloud infrastructure (setup + 3 months run)
Contingency / project management buffer (10% of labour)

assumptions: No historical actuals (real spend data) are available yet for this project; estimate is based on story points, task descriptions and standard delivery ratios, not observed velocity.
1 story point ≈ 8 person-hours of blended effort as a rough sizing heuristic, adjusted per task complexity (e.g. migration, payments, RBAC scaled up; simpler CRUD/UI tasks scaled down).

Backend Developer capacity is 1.5 FTE (~2,340 hrs over a ~6 month project at 1560 hrs/FTE-6mo); allocated 2,600 hours implies this role is the critical constraint and may need overtime, a contractor top-up, or schedule extension — flagged as a risk.

QA Engineer at 0.6 FTE (~936 hrs over 6 months) is thinly staffed relative to 24 backlog items requiring test coverage; allocated hours are tight and assume heavy reliance on automated regression rather than deep manual QA on every feature.
DevOps Engineer at 0.4 FTE is sufficient only because DevOps work is concentrated in CI/CD setup (PW-1), observability (PW-22) and decommissioning (PW-24), not continuous throughout the project.

Frontend Developer at 1.0 FTE covers the design system, dashboard, invoice UI, accessibility, responsive layout and admin back-office work; this is a significant load and is the second-most-constrained role.
Legacy data migration (PW-8, 21 points) is treated as high-risk and higher-effort per point than average due to schema mapping and data-quality issues in a 400k/2M record Oracle migration.
Payment provider integration (PW-7) includes webhook handling and reconciliation logic, estimated above the average points-to-hours ratio due to compliance and testing rigor required.
Multi-currency (PW-14) and RBAC (PW-4) are treated as complex cross-cutting features touching both backend and frontend, hence proportionally more hours than raw points would suggest.
All 24 backlog items are assumed in scope for this estimate; the Low-priority items (PW-12, PW-18, PW-19, PW-23, PW-24) are the first candidates for descoping if budget must be reduced.
Non-labour costs are estimated separately for third-party services, tooling and infrastructure not covered by the internal rate card.
A 10% contingency on labour is included given the project's technical complexity (payments, migration, compliance) and the absence of historical actuals to validate estimates.
Project timeline is assumed to be roughly 6 months of elapsed calendar time to make FTE-hour capacity comparisons meaningful.
input.reasoning: "Sizing was derived from story points as a relative complexity signal, translated to hours via an ~8hrs/point baseline, then adjusted per-task where the description indicated materially higher or lower complexity than a typical task of that size (e.g., legacy migration, payment integration, and RBAC scaled up; simple CRUD or config tasks like decommissioning or contract tests scaled down). Hours were then allocated across the four staffed roles based on task nature: backend-heavy for data/API/integration work (PW-3,4,7,8,9,10,11,13,14,17,21), frontend-heavy for UI/UX work (PW-2,5,6,15,18,19,20), QA hours layered proportionally across all features for test design and regression, and DevOps hours concentrated on PW-1, PW-22 and PW-24. Backend Developer (1.5 FTE) and Frontend Developer (1.0 FTE) hours were checked against realistic capacity over an assumed 6-month delivery window and flagged as tightly or over-subscribed given the backlog size — this is the primary schedule/cost risk. QA (0.6 FTE) and DevOps (0.4 FTE) capacities are lower but their workloads are also more concentrated, so they are less stretched proportionally. The three scenarios (P20/P50/P80) reflect uncertainty mainly driven by the legacy migration and payment integration tasks, which have the highest execution risk, plus general estimation uncertainty given no historical velocity data exists for this team. Non-labour costs cover third-party/compliance items (Stripe/PCI, accessibility audit) and infrastructure (CI/CD, migration tooling) that sit outside the internal rate card. Priority breakdown allocates the total labour+non-labour budget roughly in proportion to story points per priority tier, giving a view of where the money is going relative to backlog priority."

reductions.description: Descope the four Low-priority, non-critical-path items (PW-12 Support ticket submission, PW-18 Admin back-office, PW-19 Usage analytics, PW-23 Contract tests) to a later phase.
reductions.effect: Removes ~34 points of backlog (support ticketing, admin back-office, analytics, contract tests) from this phase, cutting associated Backend/Frontend/QA hours; core customer-facing portal and payment flow remain intact.

reductions.description: Defer PW-24 (Decommission legacy portal) until after the new portal has been live and stable for a few months.
reductions.effect: Removes ~72 hours of mixed Backend/DevOps effort from the current budget; legacy system simply keeps running a little longer at existing (already sunk) hosting cost.

reductions.description: Reduce Accessibility pass (PW-15) scope from full WCAG 2.2 AA across all screens to AA on customer-facing critical paths only (dashboard, invoices, payments) for this phase.
reductions.effect: Cuts ~60 hours of Frontend/QA effort and the external accessibility audit fee is reduced from full-app to critical-path scope.

reductions.description: Use Stripe-hosted Checkout/Elements instead of a fully custom payment UI for PW-7.
reductions.effect: Reduces Frontend and Backend integration hours by relying on Stripe's pre-built, PCI-compliant UI components rather than building custom payment forms and reconciliation UI from scratch.

reductions.description: Phase the legacy data migration (PW-8): migrate active accounts first, archive/cold-migrate the remainder in a later, separately-budgeted phase.
reductions.effect: Cuts this phase's migration effort roughly in half by deferring the long tail of inactive records and invoice history, lowering both Backend hours and migration tooling infra cost; full migration is completed in a follow-up project increment.
